adoption.notes: Reconciliation's authenticated local transport, the operator socket, landed at the current commit.

hunks.summary: The status sentence below the rendered block said the runtime implementation was in progress and not on main; it now says the runtime implements this contract without a conformance claim and shipped it in v2.5.0-rc.12, the release that froze this version.

Form (b) of reconciliation gained an exception: the answer operator-socket/v2 gives when an identical operator request finds a reconciliation recorded from commissioned feedback. That rule is operator-socket/v2's own (Idempotency and cancellation, under Tier C Reconciliation), which this version froze without. Restored in v1.

notes: Admission, dispatch, restart, reconciliation, safe defaults and decision states for a Tier C action capable of changing physical state. The runtime implements it without a conformance claim; v2.5.0-rc.12 shipped it, which froze this version. Where the Proposal section, the policy_digest row and the admission vectors name the approval_timeout_seconds runtime-config/v2 permits, they mean the deployment skill setting that version carried at the freeze revision, which the runtime at 25e0d9c read from a skill's config in its configuration, bounded by the release maximum. Draft runtime-config/v2 later dropped every deployment skill setting, so that clause now names no setting; skills-package/v3 carries the timeout as the trigger's value. That is a change to runtime-config/v2, not to this text, and this version stays as frozen.
